purpose: Teach: 精力/病棟/宿命/神父/駐留/標識/国政/故意

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: 蓮さん、患者さんの精力的な回復、嬉しい限りです。
lines.en: Ren, I'm genuinely glad to see your patient recovering so well.
lines.style: Warm, steady delivery. Honest respect in the opening. Not effusive — professional warmth that carries weight because it's earned. Clear-eyed and direct.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 病棟内の雰囲気、最近、明るくなりましたね。
lines.en: The atmosphere in the ward has really brightened lately, hasn't it?
lines.style: Gentle curiosity. Observant tone — noticing something real. Slightly hesitant, like he's offering an observation rather than stating fact. Lean into the question mark.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい。医師という宿命を、私、選んだことを、誇りに思っています。
lines.en: Yes. I chose this profession, and I'm proud of that choice.
lines.style: Measured, deliberate. Each phrase lands with quiet conviction. Not grand — humble pride. Pause before the final clause, like she's affirming something to herself as much as to him.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 病院、神父さんが、定期的に、訪問されているんですね。
lines.en: So the priest visits regularly. That's good to know.
lines.style: Gentle, observant. Small note of recognition — he's piecing something together. Not interrogative, more thoughtful. Like he's understanding the infrastructure of care around him.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい。災害地に、医療チームが駐留した経験、活きています。
lines.en: Yes. That experience — working with medical teams in disaster zones — it informs how we think about care here.
lines.style: Reflective, grounded in experience. Quiet authority. Breath under the pauses. She's drawing a line from past to present without fanfare. Tired wisdom.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 院内、新しい標識、わかりやすくて、いいですね。
lines.en: The new signage in the hospital is really clear and helpful.
lines.style: Soft observation. Almost to himself — noticing something small and good. Gentle appreciation without overstating. The tone of someone who pays attention to details others miss.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい。国政の医療政策、現場の声、もっと反映されてほしいですね。
lines.en: Yes. I wish national health policy would listen more to what we see on the ground.
lines.style: Slight frustration held steady. Not bitter, but real. Speaking from evidence, not emotion. A sigh underneath. Professional resignation that's still awake.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 故意の医療事故、報道で、目にすると、悲しくなりますね。
lines.en: When I read about preventable medical errors in the news, it really saddens me.
lines.style: Quiet, reflective close. Vulnerable — he's saying something that matters. Slow pace. Slight trailing-off, like the weight of it is settling on him. Genuine sadness, not performed.
